policy.user_agent: MedRadarBot/0.1 (+https://github.com/ChazY11/medradar; research; contact: repository owner) Python-urllib
policy.statement: Every enabled source below has a verified read path recorded in docs/radar/evidence/source_probe.json. A source whose operator refuses automated access stays disabled and is surfaced as an access restriction - it is never fetched with a spoofed identity, never retried past a refusal, and never modelled as 'nothing found'.
cannot_do: MedRadar can only read what a source publishes to anonymous readers.
No pre-publication access, no paywall, no login, no rate-limit circumvention.
Storing a title, URL and short excerpt for research citation is not a redistribution of the source's content.

access.robots: not applicable: documented public API host route

licence.name: openFDA terms of service; U.S. Government work, public domain
licence.redistribution: Bulk records are public domain; MedRadar stores identifiers, titles and official URLs with attribution.

sources.cadence_basis: openFDA declares monthly 510(k)/PMA refreshes and weekly recall refreshes; a 24h check is enough to notice a version change without polling an unchanged dataset.
sources.incremental: official endpoint version (meta.last_updated) plus a decision_date window with overlap
sources.reuses: medradar.data_pipeline.openfda (HTTP client contract), medradar.data_pipeline.model.SOURCES (endpoint + official_url catalogue)

queries.note: Querying by product code is narrower than the DATA-001 applicant sweep and returns the ~5.7k monitoring records instead of 176k 510(k) rows.

access.robots: not applicable: documented public API host route

licence.name: openFDA terms of service; U.S. Government work, public domain
licence.redistribution: Recall rows are public domain; MedRadar stores the official recall numbers, the recall event number, the product description, the reason for recall, the status and the official URL with attribution.

sources.cadence_basis: openFDA declares a weekly recall refresh; a 24h check notices a new official version within a day without polling an unchanged dataset.
sources.incremental: all-code event_date_posted window with a 30-day overlap, plus a per-product-code inventory that is repeated only when the official endpoint version changes
sources.reuses: medradar.data_pipeline.openfda (URL construction), medradar.data_pipeline.model.SOURCES (endpoint + official URL), the committed taxonomy (product codes and organisation aliases)

queries.product_codes: derived from config/radar/topics.json at run time; never a second code register
queries.window: event_date_posted:[watermark - 30d TO today], every product code, screened locally
queries.note: A row is one recalled product; an FDA recall event (res_event_number) can cover several rows, so event counts are a GROUP BY on the stored identifier, never a row count.

access.robots: E-utilities is NCBI's documented programmatic interface; without an API key the documented limit is 3 requests/second

licence.name: NCBI E-utilities usage guidelines; PubMed abstracts are public
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores PMID, title, journal, dates, authors and the official abstract URL; full text is never stored.

sources.cadence_basis: Indexing is continuous. PubMed was the only source where a 6h check can realistically surface something new the same day.
sources.incremental: Entrez date (edat) window with 3-day overlap; the watermark is the newest edat observed, never the wall clock

rate_limit.note: NCBI documented limit without an API key

access.robots: documented public REST API; api.crossref.org serves no robots.txt

licence.name: Crossref REST API terms; metadata is openly available
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores DOI, title, container title, dates and the DOI resolver URL. Crossref asks clients to identify themselves; the registry's mailto is sent on every request.

sources.cadence_basis: Crossref deposits arrive continuously from publishers; 12h keeps the check cheap.
sources.incremental: filter=from-created-date with a 2-day overlap on the newest created timestamp

rate_limit.note: polite pool; requests identify the project

access.robots: robots.txt read: the news index and the press-release paths are not disallowed (/content/ and /crsc/ are disallowed and are never fetched)

licence.name: Philips website terms; press releases are published for media use
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores the headline, publication timestamp, canonical URL and a bounded excerpt for citation. Full articles are never mirrored.

sources.cadence_basis: The news index changes only when a release is published; 12h is a politeness ceiling, not a technical limit.
sources.incremental: set difference of press-release URLs on the permitted index; content changes detected by page hash

rate_limit.note: one request every four seconds; a vendor site is not an API

access.robots: robots.txt read: the newsroom sitemap and article paths are not disallowed

licence.name: Dräger website terms; newsroom articles are published for media use
licence.redistribution: MedRadar stores the article headline, the sitemap lastmod timestamp, the canonical URL and a bounded excerpt for citation.

sources.cadence_basis: The sitemap carries a per-article lastmod, so a 12h check is sufficient and cheap.
sources.incremental: sitemap <lastmod> watermark with a 1-day overlap; new loc = NEW, newer lastmod on a known loc = UPDATED

access.robots: robots.txt itself returns HTTP 403 from the edge (Akamai 'Access Denied')
access.reason: The operator refuses anonymous automated access. This adapter ships, stays disabled, and the restriction is shown in the product as an access-policy state - never as 'no news found'. No spoofing, cookie replay or proxy was attempted.

licence.name: not determined: the operator does not serve the robots policy to this client

sources.cadence_basis: Would be 12h if access were permitted; no request is ever sent while BLOCKED.

adding_a_source: A new source is one adapter module implementing medradar.radar.adapter.SourceAdapter plus one entry here. Disabled sources are still listed so the UI can distinguish 'not monitored' from 'nothing found'.
